candidate_protocol: Candidates are scored on the development frames with the same evaluator, IoU 0.5 and the frozen score threshold recorded in regression.json; they do not re-select a threshold. A candidate that needs its own threshold is a different protocol and needs a reviewed change.
comparison: A candidate fails a gated metric when it is worse than the baseline by more than tolerance_abs x (1 + 1e-9); the 1e-9 relative margin only absorbs floating-point rounding, so exactly one count worse passes a one-count tolerance.
environment_scope: Tolerances are measured by re-running the baseline in the gating environment. Before gating a candidate in a different environment (host, ONNX Runtime, OpenCV or NumPy build), re-run the baseline there; if its detections are not bit-identical to the recorded ones, re-measure repeatability there and record it before comparing any candidate.
frozen_before_candidates: Set from the baseline and its repeat run only; no candidate model had been evaluated when this file was written.

gates.note: baseline is 0, so this gate cannot fail; it records the value only

holdout.policy: Sealed. Its frame list is frozen and hashed here, but its frames are not downloaded or evaluated before AERIS-018 release evaluation, and it never drives thresholds or model selection.

interval_note: Day-bootstrap intervals are reported as context for what the set can resolve; they are not the tolerance.

protocol.score_threshold_source: validation split, On the validation split only: the score threshold with the highest F1 at IoU 0.5 on the grid 0.01, 0.02, ..., 0.99; ties go to the higher threshold. If no grid value gives a true positive, the threshold is null and the gate is blocked.

tolerance_rationale: For each gated metric: max(2 x the largest absolute difference observed between the baseline run and the repeat run, the metric's resolution floor). A candidate fails when it is worse than the baseline by more than the tolerance. COCO reports AP to three decimals; smaller differences are below reporting resolution. A single object or detection changing state is the smallest real change on a fixed frame set. A width bin with fewer than 30 scored objects, or a negative-frame metric with fewer than 30 negative frames, is reported as not gated (unavailable), never as a pass.
